passage.title: Teacher-written article for TGA
paras: Trophies tarnish. Titles pass to others. What lasts is harder to see: habits handed on, people helped, examples that others copy without knowing where they came from. A legacy is less a monument than a seed. The people we remember longest are often those who adapted when plans failed, served when no one was watching, and gave credit away.

head: Article idea
Ali
Umar
Khalid
rows: built new systems for a growing state
withdrew at Mu'tah to save the army
lived simply; cared for the needy
inspired people who stand by beliefs
the Hijri calendar still used today

model.title: Write one sentence that synthesises the article and two lives

parts.text: Article idea: legacy is a seed
Life 1: Umar's calendar still orders Muslim life
Life 2: Khalid's sincerity is still taught
Synthesis connective: Both..., which supports the article's view that...

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: Both Umar and Khalid left seeds rather than monuments: Umar's calendar still orders Muslim life and Khalid's sincerity is still taught, which supports the article's view that legacy grows in others.

keywords.def: combining ideas from different texts into one answer
changing your approach when circumstances change
what you give to help something succeed
judge how true or important something is

questions.q: Summarise the article in one sentence
questions.a: Lasting legacy comes from service, adaptability and helping others, not from trophies or titles.

questions.q: Which word means changing your approach?
Core: in the portal response box, write a synthesis paragraph: What creates a lasting legacy? Use the article and two biographies. Starter: 'Lasting legacy comes from...'
Extend: evaluate: does the article ignore the role of victories? Explain
Stretch: write an admired sentence from any text and explain why you admire it
What does 'a legacy is less a monument than a seed' suggest?
options: legacy grows in other people over time
questions.a: B) legacy grows in other people over time. A seed grows into something new; a monument stays still. The writer means legacy lives on through others.

questions.q: The article suggests legacy is like...
Answer the ponder in one sentence
questions.a: For example: What we gave, because gifts grow in other people.
